steps.summary: Implement atomic, validated, persistent snapshots with bounded stale age and Windows-safe replacement.
Implement one upstream client with separated timeouts, bounded retries, conditional requests, structured errors, and circuit state.
Persist shard and champion sources, restore on startup, and serve controlled snapshot/stale results when public sources fail.
Persist champion lookup and per-hero ARAM last-known-good payloads while preserving singleflight and image caching.
Persist the existing bounded ban-query last-known-good cache across service restarts.
Return a final text/image/forward delivery envelope so GroupGuard does not parse business data.
Expose per-source live/cache/snapshot/stale/unavailable state, age, error class, and circuit state.
Add service, fixture, and pinned cross-repository contract tests including restart and no-public-network scenarios.
Deploy the backward-compatible service release before any GroupGuard runtime migration.

current_findings.summary: Generic JSON loading performs one request with one timeout and no retry, error classification, or snapshot fallback.
Shard and champion sources are memory-only and both public sources are required again after restart or expiry.
ARAM payloads and champion lookup have no persistent last-known-good data.
The bounded stale ban cache exists but is lost on restart.
Current endpoints return business data or raw images but no uniform final delivery envelope for GroupGuard.

next_recommended_action.condition: Run after PR #9 passes Windows CI and review.
next_recommended_action.summary: Build the shared upstream HTTP client before integrating snapshots into shard queries.

production_rule: The service release must remain compatible with the currently deployed GroupGuard, must be deployed first, and must pass restart plus upstream-failure acceptance before plugin migration.
